brief: Goldman Sachs TMT specialist Peter Callahan recaps Day 2 of the GS Communacopia and Technology Conference. The desk reads the week as upbeat (healthy consumer soundbites, steady enterprise demand, tight semi supply/demand) but reports a standing tension: bottom-up datapoints remain very constructive, juxtaposed against top-down debates that are an output of summer volatility, rates and geopolitical uncertainty, midterm policy uncertainty and the law of large numbers, so investors hesitate to fully re-commit to the AI infrastructure trade. Company takeaways feed the bottom-up side. Dell framed AI as a multi-year infrastructure S-curve with enterprises only beginning to move past productivity tools, cited 6,500 AI Factory customers, ~400mn PCs over four years old and ~1.3mn servers on 13G or older platforms as replacement demand still ahead, and sees component availability possibly worse in 2027 than 2026. Salesforce (~5% of customers on AE1, ~60-80% uplift) and ServiceNow (4.5x original contract value per seat) frame AI monetization as an installed-base upgrade. Etsy and Walmart describe agentic commerce traffic as small but high intent. The Day 3 preview lists stock-level debates for NVDA, DDOG, MDB, UBER, SPCX, CRDO, LRCX and STX. The note reports and previews, it does not argue one market call.
